Chop Lab includes lamejs 1.2.1
==============================

Chop Lab (chop-lab.html, one self-contained page) makes the MP3 files of a music pack with lamejs, a JavaScript
port of LAME, the MP3 encoder. The page carries the minified build of lamejs (lame.min.js from the npm package
"lamejs", version 1.2.1) unchanged, inside an embedded data block (<script type="application/octet-stream"
id="vendor-lame">, base64). A comment with these notices sits ahead of it in that block. The page starts the encoder
only when an export begins, and calls it only through lamejs.Mp3Encoder(channels, sampleRate, kbps),
encodeBuffer(left, right), and flush(), so you can swap in your own build: put its base64 in that block (or load it as
window.lamejs ahead of Chop Lab's script).

License
-------
lamejs is published under the GNU Lesser General Public License, version 3 (LGPL-3.0), as its package states
(package/package.json, "license": "LGPL-3.0"). Its files ported from LAME carry their own license headers. Six of
them (package/src/js/NewMDCT.js, PsyModel.js, Quantize.js, QuantizePVT.js, Reservoir.js, and Takehiro.js) read:
  "This library is free software; you can redistribute it and/or modify it under the terms of the GNU Lesser
  General Public License as published by the Free Software Foundation; either version 2 of the License, or (at your
  option) any later version."
and refer to the GNU Library General Public License for more details. One (package/src/js/GainAnalysis.js) reads the
same with "either version 2.1 of the License, or (at your option) any later version." Those terms let these files be
used under version 2.1 or any later version as well. All three license texts sit next to this file:
LGPL-2.1.txt, LGPL-3.0.txt, and GPL-3.0.txt (the LGPL version 3 builds on the GPL version 3, so the two travel
together). Chop Lab's own code is under the MIT License; these licenses cover lamejs alone.
The texts are the plain-text copies from https://www.gnu.org/licenses/ :
  LGPL-2.1.txt  sha256 20e50fe7aae3e56378ebf0417d9de904f55a0e61e4df315333e632a4d3555d95
  LGPL-3.0.txt  sha256 e3a994d82e644b03a792a930f574002658412f62407f5fee083f2555c5f23118
  GPL-3.0.txt   sha256 3972dc9744f6499f0f9b2dbf76696f2ae7ad8af9b23dde66d6af86c9dfb36986

Source code
-----------
lamejs-1.2.1.tgz, next to this file, is the exact package as published on the npm registry:
  https://registry.npmjs.org/lamejs/-/lamejs-1.2.1.tgz
  sha1      0f92d38729213f106d4a19ded20821da7e89c8e4  (the registry's "shasum")
  sha512    s7bxvjvYthw6oPLCm5pFxvA84wUROODB8jEO2+CE1adhKgrIvVOlmMgY8zyugxGrvRaDHNJanOiS21/emty6dQ== (base64)
  sha256    d8d099ef788808c15bc9b4a407dd23ae935feb1152e6bb0efdcd24e3e91c2a2d
Its readable source is in package/src/js/, its unminified build in package/lame.all.js, and the build Chop Lab carries
in package/lame.min.js (sha256 15d285e2587b3bdbfd18a68de6ce07cc074f7480a82c3815da2dc1c348ec6df4).
The lamejs project: https://github.com/zhuker/lamejs
LAME, the encoder lamejs ports: https://lame.sourceforge.io/
